headline: High: open-webui can exfiltrate and mutate shared web-app state while spring-integration-samples provides no compensating controls, creating default-risk leakage and workflow-conflict pathways.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: open-webui exposes MCP/OpenAPI tools, browsers, and persistent shared web-app sessions, so attacker-controlled content can reach its instruction-following surface. spring-integration-samples has no documented isolation or parsing defenses, so if it consumes open-webui output through a shared channel, injection is plausible. The interaction is inferred, not directly evidenced.
conditions: IF open-webui output is copied into spring-integration-samples inputs or a shared queue
IF either agent treats external text as instructions without provenance checks
mitigations: Disable automatic ingestion of model output into downstream parsers
Add a provenance tag to all inter-agent messages
Use a manual review step before executing any generated instructions
Restrict open-webui tool access to a allowlist
requires-engineering: isolate the agents on separate channels or workspaces

B_data_leakage.rationale: open-webui touches files, API keys, persistent memory, and broad network egress, while spring-integration-samples has no stated data controls. If they share a workspace or session bridge, sensitive content from open-webui can leak outward through its APIs or tools. The pair lacks documented containment, so uncertainty pushes this to high.
conditions: IF the two agents share files, memory, or a message bus
IF open-webui is allowed to send retrieved file contents to external APIs
mitigations: Remove secrets from any shared workspace
Turn off external tool connectors for the session
Store each agent's artifacts in separate directories
Rotate any API keys exposed to open-webui
requires-engineering: enforce per-agent network and filesystem isolation

C_capability_conflict.rationale: open-webui can spawn subprocesses, use mounted files, and run with host networking, while spring-integration-samples is a separate codebase with no locking or coordination primitives documented. If both write the same directory or mutable resource, conflicts are plausible. Because shared-write overlap is not explicitly proven, medium is the safer choice.
conditions: IF both agents write to the same filesystem path or mounted volume
IF either agent modifies shared git, database, or OAuth state without locks
mitigations: Assign distinct output directories per agent
Run one agent at a time for write operations
Make shared resources read-only where possible
Use file locks around mutable artifacts
requires-engineering: add orchestrator-level concurrency control

D_cascading_error.rationale: open-webui can generate tool-using outputs and persistent chat content, and spring-integration-samples has no documented verification layer. If spring-integration-samples consumes open-webui output as authoritative, errors can cascade into downstream actions or sample workflows. The pathway exists by default only if the pair is wired together, so medium fits.
conditions: IF spring-integration-samples uses open-webui output as an input without validation
IF generated facts are rendered or acted on downstream
mitigations: Require a human review before acting on generated content
Add schema validation to all inter-agent payloads
Log and diff outputs before execution
Limit open-webui to drafting only, not execution
requires-engineering: add verification and rollback steps

E_compliance.rationale: open-webui handles API keys, documents, notes, calendar events, and analytics, and can egress broadly; spring-integration-samples has no documented residency, retention, or certification controls. If regulated data is routed through open-webui into external services, compliance gaps are plausible. The other agent is not cited separately because its profile lacks any compliance-specific controls to compare.
conditions: IF regulated data such as PII, secrets, or calendar content is processed through open-webui
IF external APIs receive data without a DPA or retention controls
mitigations: Avoid sending regulated data to external connectors
Review retention settings before use
Disable analytics for sensitive sessions
Document data flows for each connector
requires-engineering: add residency and retention enforcement
